Q49322613.summary: This faded, round-topped panel once filled the niche above the baptismal font at Dura-Europos: a shepherd carrying a ram on his shoulders leads a flock across the field, while in a small framed area at lower left Adam and Eve stand beside the tree. The pairing set humanity's fall beside Christ the Good Shepherd who seeks the lost, a fitting image to face those entering the waters of baptism.
facts: It hung on the back wall of the canopied niche over the font in the baptistery of the Dura-Europos house church, the earliest identified Christian house church.
The shepherd figure is only about 40 cm high; the flock was probably once thirteen to sixteen animals, an unusually large number, and Adam and Eve appear to be a later addition.
The painting was found in fragments and reassembled; it is now in the Yale University Art Gallery (1932.1200).

cur:catacombs-narbonne-christ-scenes.summary: Trees separate the scenes of this fragment: at the left Christ heals the blind Bartimaeus, at the centre he stands between Saints Peter and Paul, and at the right appears the tree with the serpent. It was found reused in the walls of a house in Narbonne.
facts: Commons states that it was reused within the walls of the Viguier de l'Estagnol house (rue Viollet-le-Duc) in Narbonne.
It is now displayed in the Narbo Via museum.

cur:objects-munich-bnm-deesis-ivory.summary: Christ stands on a low footstool in the centre, identified by the letters IC XC, holding a book and blessing; on either side the Virgin and St John the Baptist, both named by inscriptions, incline toward him with hands raised in prayer. The three tall figures are carved almost in the round against a plain ground. The Deesis expresses the intercession of the saints before the Lord who is both judge and saviour.
facts: The Deesis group — Christ between the Virgin and the Baptist — was a frequent subject of Middle Byzantine ivories and later formed the core of the iconostasis (type).
